newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Novus says Sumatra well in production.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Novus says Sumatra well in production.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Wednesday that the Aryani A-1 oil well in south east Sumatra, Indonesia, in which it has a 3.72 percent stake, began producing on February 15 at the rate of more than 2,700 barrels a day.
The Aryani Development is the fifth field to be developed in the area using a low cost monotower option, Novus said.
Aryani-1, which was drilled in October 1989, encountered a seven metre net oil pay in a sand of the Talang Akar formation and the well was suspended as a possible future producer.
"At the time, this relatively small accumulation was considered likely to be sub-economic," Novus said.

"However, its commercial viability has been transformed by the low cost development options now available and the decision was made to develop this field along with other so called marginal fields such as Chesy and Vita," the company said.
A monotower was set on the Aryani-1 location in December and in February the well was re-entered and completed as Aryani A-1.

Other partners are Maxus Energy Corp subsidiary Maxus Southeast Sumatra (operator) 55.68 percent, Inpex Sumatra 13.07 percent, Deminex Sumatra 5.00 percent, Repsol 9.87 percent, Warner International 3.77 percent and CIECO Sumatra 8.91 percent. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-3 9373-1800
